Aurvandil's Toe.t: In Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda, Thor carries Aurvandill in a basket across the icy rivers Élivágar. One toe sticks out and freezes, and Thor breaks it off and throws it into the sky as a star. The Edda does not say which star: Sirius and Venus have both been guessed. Stellarium's Norse figures put it in Corona Borealis.
Aurvandil's Toe.c: Snorri Sturluson, Skáldskaparmál (13th century), as summarised in Wikipedia, “Aurvandill”

Woman's Cart.t: The Little Dipper as a wagon: the women's wagon, beside the men's wagon of the Big Dipper, as the North Germanic languages still name the pair.

Man's Cart.t: The Big Dipper as a wagon. In the North Germanic languages it is still the men's wagon (Karlavagnen in Swedish, Karlsvogna in Norwegian), and the Little Dipper is the women's; Norse pagans are also said to have called it Odin's wagon.
